questions.q: Why can a tax on a good be regressive?
options: Poorer people spend a larger share of their income on it
Rich people pay more of it

questions.q: A minimum price set above equilibrium is likely to cause:
options: A fall in the market price
questions.why: At the higher price, more is supplied and less is demanded.

questions.q: Unlike an indirect tax, a minimum price raises no revenue for the government.
questions.why: The extra money goes to sellers.

questions.q: Explain how a subsidy could correct the under-consumption of a good with external benefits.

ideas.label: The subsidy lowers firms' costs or the price
So consumption rises towards the social optimum

questions.model: A subsidy lowers the costs of firms, so the price falls. People consume more, which moves the market towards the social optimum.
questions.why: It works just like a tax in reverse.

tests.answer: It lowers the price so people consume more, moving towards the social optimum.
